text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English poet and satirist ALEXANDER POPE was born on this day in 1688.
Australian motorcyle star TOMMY BENSTEAD was born in 1896.
American jazz pianist and composer THOMAS "FATS" WALLER was born in 1904.
Russian civil rights campaigner ANDREI SAKHAROV, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965, was born in 1921.
Former Australian Prime Minister MALCOLM FRASER was born in 1930.
Australian swimmer JON KONRADS, who once held 26 world records, was born in 1942.

British singer/songwriter LEO SAYER, who was promoted and made into a star by ADAM FAITH (a rockstar of the 1960's), was born in 1948. His hits included "The Show Must Go On" (1973), "Long Tall Glasses" (1974), "You Make Me Feel Like Dancing"(1976), "When I Need You" (1977) and "More Than I Can Say" (1980).
The one-time 'darling' of "Young Talent Time", SALLY BOYDEN, was born in 1965.
** EVENTS **
1471 : KING HENRY VI of England died in the Tower of
London, thought to have been the victim of murder instigated by KING EDWARD IV.
1542 : HERNANDO de SOTO, Spanish explorer of South
America and what were to become the southeastern states of the U.S., died.
1840 : New Zealand was proclaimed a British colony.
1879 : During conflict between Peru and Chile a naval
battle took place off the coast of Iquique. The town was eventually transferred to Chilean hands.
1924 : Two Chicago teenagers kidnapped and murdered 14
year-old BOBBY FRANKS. The 19 year-old youths, RICHARD LOEB and NATHAN LEOPOLD, were sons of millionaires, and confessed to the killing, which they said was carried-out for a "thrill".
1927 : CHARLES LINDBERG landed his plane in Paris,
winning a 25,000 dollar prize for the first solo flight across the Atlantic. The flight, in his specially built aircraft "Spirit of St Louis", took 33 hours and 40 minutes.
1964 : A BBC survey showed that the 'Beatles' were
Britain's most popular tourist attraction.
1966 : CASSIUS CLAY, who later changed his name to
Muhammad Ali, retained the world heavyweight boxing crown, knocking-down challenger HENRY COOPER in the 6th round of their bout in London.
1977 : An opinion poll on a proposed new national anthem
for Australia was easily won by "Advance Australia Fair".
1979 : ELTON JOHN played a concert in Leningrad, becoming
the first western rock star to perform in the USSR.
1980 : "The Clash" guitarist JOE STRUMMER was arrested at
a concert in Hamburg after smashing his instrument over the head of one of the audience.
1982 : In the Falklands War, British troops established a
bridgehead at Port San Carlos and HMS Ardent was sunk with the loss of 22 lives.
1989 : A million people, a sixth of the population of
Hong Kong, demonstrated in support of rebellious students in Peking.
1990 : ION ILESCU won the first free elections in
Romania.
1991 : Ethiopia's military strongman MENGISTU HAILE
MARIAM stepped down and flew to exile after 14 years of brutal rule.
1991 : Former Indian Prime Minister RAJIV GANDHI was
assassinated, blown up by a woman terrorist (who had a bomb strapped to her body) at an election rally in the country's South.
1994 : BAKILI MULUZI was sworn in as Malawi's president
and quickly moved to erase the worst excesses of defeated president KAMUZU BANDA's 30-year single-party rule.
